title: Strict normal crossings divisors over a field
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $p:V\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ a smooth finite-type scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A quasi-coherent ideal $I$ defines a strict normal crossings divisor if it is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] and radical (so its closed subscheme is reduced [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]), and there are finitely many pairwise distinct integral closed subschemes $C_i\subset V$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose supports have union $|V(I)|$, such that every scheme-theoretic intersection $C_J=\bigcap_{i\in J}C_i$ is smooth over $F$ and of codimension $|J|$ in $V$. Scheme-theoretic intersections are defined by sums of the ideals. Codimension here means $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{C_J,z}+|J|$ at every point of $C_J$, using ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. These $C_i$ are exactly the reduced irreducible components. For $J=\varnothing$ the intersection is $V$; the empty divisor and empty family of components are allowed. The same component formula defines the predicate for an arbitrary structure morphism $p$.
